newsitem.title: USA: Dow industrials off lows, Nasdaq up.
newsitem.headline: Dow industrials off lows, Nasdaq up.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks pulled themselves off early lows in mixed trading Wednesday, withstanding a bout of profit-taking that followed yesterday's dramatic rise, analysts said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which bounced back Tuesday from steep losses on Monday, was down five points at 7752. Early in the session it was down nearly 50 points.
The Nasdaq composite was up 3.38 points at 1455.
Stocks were jostled as money managers adjusted their stock portfolios ahead of the end of the quarter, analysts said.

"The feeling is that the second quarter is going to be pretty good and that all of the bad news has already been pre-announced," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "But there has been some profit-taking and a lot of portfolio realignment."
Other analysts said the stock market was also hampered by a sluggish bond market.
"The bond market is looking tired," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "With stocks at these levels, shares need the support of bonds."
The long bond was down 11/32 at a 6.72 percent yield.
